purpose: Independent practice of D1.4 — ordering categories by frequency.
student_learning_goal: I can order categories from greatest to least.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can order categories from greatest to least.
header.character_watermark: Tally the Tally Cat in the top-right corner pointing to a pictograph with arrows. Small (~1.5in tall). References blueprint.recurring_characters.

parts.student_instructions: Look at each pictograph. Circle the GREATEST row. Underline the LEAST row.
parts.visual_layout: Three small pictographs stacked vertically. Each pictograph has 3-4 rows. Row counts: Pictograph 1 — Apples 4, Bananas 6, Grapes 2. Pictograph 2 — Sunny 7, Rainy 4, Snowy 2. Pictograph 3 — Soccer 5, Tag 3, Hockey 6, Hopscotch 1. Each pictograph ~5in × 1.5in.

image_placeholders.description: Three small pictographs stacked vertically for a Grade 1 worksheet, B&W line art. Each pictograph has a title and labels. Pictograph 1 (Favourite Fruit): apples (4), bananas (6), grapes (2) — 3 rows. Pictograph 2 (Weather Last Week): sunny (7), rainy (4), snowy (2) — 3 rows. Pictograph 3 (Recess Game): soccer (5), tag (3), hockey (6), hopscotch (1) — 4 rows. Each pictograph ~5in × 1.5in. Pictures evenly sized.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS04_P1_PICTOGRAPHS at Part 1: instructions ask the child to identify greatest and least. Keywords name the visual elements (pictographs) and the response criteria (greatest, least).

parts.answer_key: Pictograph 1: greatest = bananas, least = grapes. Pictograph 2: greatest = sunny, least = snowy. Pictograph 3: greatest = hockey, least = hopscotch.

parts.part_title: Part 2: Order from greatest to least.
parts.student_instructions: Look at the tally chart. Order the categories from greatest (1) to least (4). Number them.
parts.visual_layout: A tally chart with 4 categories: 'Favourite Animal' — Dog ||||CROSS || (7), Cat ||||CROSS (5), Bird || (2), Fish ||||CROSS ||| (8). Beside each row, a blank box for the order number 1-4.

image_placeholders.description: A 4-row tally chart for a Grade 1 worksheet, B&W line art. Title: 'Favourite Animal'. Rows: Dog with ||||CROSS || (7), Cat with ||||CROSS (5), Bird with || (2), Fish with ||||CROSS ||| (8). Each row has a label, tally area, total, and an empty number box for ordering. Total chart ~5in × 2in.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS04_P2_TALLY at Part 2: instructions ask the child to order categories. Keywords name the data source (tally) and the ordering rule (order, greatest).

parts.answer_key: Fish = 1 (greatest at 8). Dog = 2 (7). Cat = 3 (5). Bird = 4 (least at 2).

parts.part_title: Part 3: Build and order a pictograph.
parts.student_instructions: Use this data: 4 hockey, 7 soccer, 3 baseball. Build a pictograph. Then order the rows by greatest to least.
parts.visual_layout: A blank pictograph grid with 3 rows. Above: title line. Beside each row: label box and an order number box (1-3). The child draws the pictures, labels rows, and orders.

image_placeholders.description: A blank pictograph grid for a Grade 1 worksheet, B&W line art. ~5in × 3in with 3 empty rows. Each row has a label box on the left, ~7 grid cells in the middle for picture placement, and a small number box on the right for the order. Above the grid, a thin title line. Designed for the child to build a pictograph from given data and order it.
image_placeholders.text_image_alignment_check: Image WS04_P3_GRID at Part 3: instructions ask the child to build and order a pictograph. Keywords name the format (pictograph) and the ordering task (order).

parts.answer_key: Title: 'Favourite Sport' (or similar). Hockey row: 4 pictures, order = 2. Soccer row: 7 pictures, order = 1 (greatest). Baseball row: 3 pictures, order = 3 (least).

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, write a sentence: 'The greatest in this graph is ___.'
teacher_notes: Lesson 4 consolidation artifact. Use Part 2 as the formative signal for the position-not-count trap — children who order by tally COUNT, not by row position, have mastered the rule.
